transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

To answer your question: it could be either. A flashing red light on a Dyson V10 usually means the battery protection system has triggered (often due to a blockage causing overheating) or that the battery itself is failing to accept a charge. It doesn't necessarily mean the whole machine is dead. To narrow this down, please check the charging behaviour: when you place the vacuum on its charger (or plug the charger directly into it), does a solid red light come on to show it is charging, or do the lights flash immediately? If you see a solid light, leave it for 30 minutes and try again. If it flashes straight away, we likely have a battery or charger issue.

No solid red light at all. When it's on the charger the blue lights come on, then it sometimes shows the flashing red too. When I press the trigger it's definitely flashing red, about once a second, and the motor doesn't try to start. Battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly, if that matters.

That pattern—blue lights on charge but flashing red when you try to start, with no motor engagement—is classic battery protection mode. Since it didn't charge properly (no solid red), one of two things is happening: either the charger/dock isn't delivering power, or the battery has a dead cell that trips its internal safety. To separate these, please check the charger itself: unplug the wall-end from your current socket and plug it into a different, known-working socket. Does the light on the charger brick (the boxy part) stay solid red? If the charger light flashes or stays off, replace the charger.
If the charger light is solid red but the vacuum still flashes red when you press the trigger, the battery has likely failed internally and needs replacing.

I tried the hallway socket as well and the light on the charger is on, but I get the same result: still flashing red when I press the trigger. I also left it charging for a good 3.5 hours or more with the charger plugged straight into the battery, and the blue lights came on but it still flashes red. So is the battery done?

[Heading: Likely cause: battery — flat or failed (cordless)]
Yes, the evidence points to a failed battery. You will need to replace the battery pack. Dyson offers replacement batteries directly; if yours is within warranty, contact them first.
